newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian companies plan 300 mln pound cement plant.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian companies plan 300 mln pound cement plant.

text.p: Egyptian state companies are working on plans to build a cement plant in south Egypt at a cost of 300 million pounds and will offer the public a 30 percent stake, an official close to the project said on Monday.

"Within two or three months a new company will be set up and take decisions about such issues as offering tenders," director of the investment department at National Bank of Egypt, Nadir Ezzeddin, told Reuters.
The founders have acquired a free plot for the plant, which will have an annual capacity of 1.2 million tonnes, in Qena province, 450 km (280 miles) south of Cairo, Ezzeddin said.
The founders, including the National Bank, the Holding Company for Housing and Construction and two insurance companies, will hold 70 percent of the new company, he added.
The other nine million of the company's 30 million shares will be offered to the public at a price of 10.00 pounds each, a quarter of which is payable initially.
The project will employ about 1,000 people, Ezzeddin said.
